hints: Focus on tracking moles, not grams, since the change in ethanoic acid tells you how far the equilibrium has shifted.
Calculate initial moles of each reactant and the equilibrium moles of acid, then use the 1:1:1:1 stoichiometry to find the change in ester.
Recall how temperature affects an exothermic equilibrium and what, other than temperature, can or cannot change the value of Kc.
walkthrough:
**Find initial moles and equilibrium change**

Start by converting all masses to moles. This is an esterification with 1:1:1:1 stoichiometry, so every mole of acid used makes one mole of ester.

$$n = \frac{m}{M_r}$$
$$n(\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{OH}) = \frac{9.2}{46} = 0.20 \text{ mol}$$
$$n(\text{CH}_3\text{CO}_2\text{H})_{initial} = \frac{12}{60} = 0.20 \text{ mol}$$
$$n(\text{CH}_3\text{CO}_2\text{C}_2\text{H}_5)_{initial} = \frac{8.8}{88} = 0.10 \text{ mol}$$

**Check statement 1 using ICE logic**

At equilibrium at 298 K, acid is 4.8 g.

$$n(\text{CH}_3\text{CO}_2\text{H})_{eqm} = \frac{4.8}{60} = 0.08 \text{ mol}$$
Acid has decreased by $0.20 - 0.08 = 0.12$ mol, so the forward reaction has occurred by 0.12 mol. Ester must increase by the same amount.

$$n(\text{ester})_{eqm} = 0.10 + 0.12 = 0.22 \text{ mol}$$
So statement 1 is correct.

**Check statement 2 with Le Chatelier**

The forward reaction is exothermic, $\Delta H^\ominus = -6 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$.

$$\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{OH} + \text{CH}_3\text{CO}_2\text{H} \rightleftharpoons \text{CH}_3\text{CO}_2\text{C}_2\text{H}_5 + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$
Increasing temperature to 323 K favours the endothermic direction, which is the backward reaction. Equilibrium shifts left, so more ethanoic acid remains than at 298 K. So statement 2 is correct.

**Check statement 3 about Kc**

The equilibrium constant $K_c$ depends only on temperature, not on concentration.

$$K_c = \frac{[\text{CH}_3\text{CO}_2\text{C}_2\text{H}_5][\text{H}_2\text{O}]}{[\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{OH}][\text{CH}_3\text{CO}_2\text{H}]}$$
Adding water at the start will shift the position to the left, but at the same temperature the ratio at the new equilibrium returns to the same $K_c$ value. So statement 3 is correct.

**Conclude**

Since 1, 2 and 3 are all correct, choose the option that lists all three.

options.A: Correct. Statement 1 is true (0.22 mol ester by ICE calculation), statement 2 is true (higher T shifts exothermic equilibrium left, giving more acid), and statement 3 is true (Kc changes only with temperature).
options.B: Incorrect. This combination leaves out statement 3. Students choose this if they think adding a product changes Kc, but Kc is unaffected by concentration changes at constant temperature.
options.C: Incorrect. This combination leaves out statement 1. Students choose this if they make an arithmetic slip with moles or forget to add the initial 0.10 mol of ester to the 0.12 mol formed.
options.D: Incorrect. This combination leaves out statements 2 and 3. It suggests confusion over Le Chatelier for an exothermic reaction and over the temperature-only dependence of Kc.
